Hi all —

Detailed answers below; I call out exceptions so you can judge whether the 48–96h window holds for CapitalWave's workload.

1) Stages and typical timing (normal case):
   - Tombstone creation (t0): immediate when deletion triggered — metadata written to primary within seconds.
   - Primary GC / local expunge (t0 + 0–2h): primary node expunges local copies according to retention policy and tombstone queue.
   - Regional replica sweep (t0 + 2–24h): replicas process tombstones in order; typical propagation completes within a day in healthy regions.
   - Offsite/archive sweep (t0 + 24–96h): archival layer (cold copies) is marked for purge and a scheduled job expires content; full physical expunge depends on archive batching windows (daily) and downstream retention queues — can take up to 4 days in worst-case backpressure.

Notes: network partitions or large backlog can extend the tail (we've seen rare cases up to 7 days during multi-region incidents). Cross-region failover may stall replica progression until re-sync completes.

2) Legal hold behavior:
   - We support account-level legal holds. When enabled, expunge jobs are prevented from final deletion (archive purge is skipped) and tombstones are retained with a hold flag. Active reads from the primary remain unaffected. Holds are visible in the audit export.

3) Audit artifacts we provide:
   - expunge_job_id (string)
   - tombstone_id (string) with associated object_path
   - timestamp events: tombstone_created, replica_processed_at[region], archive_purge_scheduled, archive_purge_completed
   - replica ids and region tags

We can produce a CSV that includes the above fields for any deletion window you request. Example attached is a synthetic extract that mirrors the format we export.

4) Practical recommendations for CapitalWave:
   - If you have short legal-response SLAs, request enabling account-level legal holds for sensitive datasets preemptively when deletions are initiated.
   - For high-sensitivity data, prefer immediate snapshot retention (WORM-like snapshot) for the hold duration to avoid waiting on archive purge cycles.
   - Schedule a joint runbook review with our Ops team if you expect >1000 expunge events/day — backpressure can materially extend timelines.

If you'd like, I can produce an audit extract for the last 90 days for a sample dataset so your audit team can verify the fields we provide.

-Karthik
